findings.evidence: `virtualCharacters` is `AddSubgroup.closure (Set.range FDRep.character)` (CharacterTable/VirtualCharacter.lean:101) with generation principle `virtualCharacters_le` (line 114), and `indClassFunAddHom` is additive, so the two closures coincide with no hypothesis on `k`. Grep confirms no such lemma exists: the only equalities involving `indVirtualCharacters` in the repo are `indVirtualCharacters_eq_virtualCharacters_iff` (Ideal.lean:247) and `indVirtualCharacters_eq_indCharacterSpanInt` (Artin.lean:255).
findings.fix: Add the hypothesis-free characterization next to `indVirtualCharacters_le_iff`: `indVirtualCharacters k G P = AddSubgroup.closure {f | ∃ S : Subgroup G, P S ∧ ∃ V : FDRep k S, indClassFun S V.character = f}`. `≥` is `AddSubgroup.closure_le` with `indClassFun_mem_indVirtualCharacters hS (character_mem_virtualCharacters V)`; `≤` is `indVirtualCharacters_le_iff.mpr` plus `virtualCharacters_le` on the comap along `indClassFunAddHom S`.
findings.issue: `indVirtualCharacters k G P` is the closure of induced *virtual* characters, but the roadmap product (README Layer 6: "the ℤ-membership of |G| • χ in the subgroup generated by cyclic-induced characters"; `Suggested.lean:295` pins `AddSubgroup.closure {f | ∃ C, IsCyclic C ∧ ∃ ψ : FDRep k C, f = indClassFun ψ.character}`) is the closure of induced *characters*, a priori smaller. The only bridge this PR exposes is `indVirtualCharacters_eq_indCharacterSpanInt` (Artin.lean:255), which requires `[IsAlgClosed k]` and `∀ C, P C → IsUnit (Nat.card C : k)`, so a consumer cannot get the roadmap's form from `natCard_nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic` without redoing the generation argument.

summary: Compatibility surface is clean and the new bundled maps carry their characterizing simp lemmas, but the canonical endpoint `indVirtualCharacters` is never identified with the subgroup generated by induced genuine characters — the object the roadmap names — except through a comparison gated on `[IsAlgClosed k]` and subgroup-order invertibility that the underlying fact does not need.
